note: How many things a text asks the candidate for. One rule, two implementations, because it is
checks a written bank, and `count_asks` in apps/ai-worker/readi_worker/interview/asks.py stops
the phrasing call adding an ask to a question at run time. Both assert against this file, so the
two copies cannot drift - check-bank fails on a mismatch like any other error, and
tests/test_interview_asks.py fails on the same one. Verified on 2026-09-26 to agree on every
prompt and probe in /content/seed as well.
The counter over-counts on purpose-built prose and that is documented, not a bug: see the
`over-counts` cases. It is used as a floor and as a comparison between two near-identical texts,
never as an absolute ceiling - `check-bank.mjs` has its own narrower check for that.
An ASYMMETRY, though, is a bug, because the comparison is what the guard runs on: if the bank's
wording and a faithful rephrasing of it count differently, the guard rejects the rephrasing. The
second paid run found two, and the `asymmetry` cases below are them.

cases.text: This is the code that moves it, in JavaScript.
What is the exception telling you?
How would you order the testing?
Would you take it?

cases.why: over-counts: the directive-owns rule covers `tell/walk/talk/take me`, not `explain`
cases.text: Explain what that check actually proves.

cases.why: a directive owns the interrogative that follows it
cases.text: Tell me what is actually in that copy.
Walk me through what happens to that error.

cases.why: the house depth cue asks for nothing new
cases.text: Which is the more serious? Take me through it.

cases.why: …and a prompt that is nothing but the cue still asks one thing
cases.text: Walk me through it.

cases.why: a cue with a noun in it is the ask, and is counted
cases.text: Walk me through what you would change.
Which is the more serious, and what makes it so?

cases.why: three, which is what the retrofit of 2026-09-25 removed
cases.text: Walk me through how that state comes about, what you would change, and what you would do about the rows that are already wrong.

cases.why: an interrogative owns a following modal: one ask, not two
cases.text: What would you change?

cases.why: but a bare modal of its own is an ask
cases.text: What is in that copy, and would you take it?

cases.why: over-counts: `where` is a relative pronoun here, not an interrogative
cases.text: Support have found accounts where money left one and never arrived in the other. Walk me through how that state comes about.
Explain what the check that is there does, and what it does not do.

cases.why: asymmetry fixed 2026-09-26: `whom` was not counted, so this read as one ask while a model's "and who it affects" read as two, and the guard rejected the rephrasing three times
cases.text: What is going wrong, and for whom?

cases.why: …and the rephrasing it was rejecting. The two must agree
cases.text: What's going wrong here, and who it affects.

cases.why: asymmetry fixed 2026-09-26: `whether` is a subordinator here, not an interrogative, so this is the one ask the bank wrote
cases.text: Talk me through something you built, whether that was at work or on your own.

cases.why: …and the pinned wording it has to match
cases.text: Take me through something you built — anything, at work or on your own.

cases.why: a directive already owns a `whether` that follows it
cases.text: Tell me whether it had been worth doing.
